22.1.title: Diagram-to-code component map
22.1.analysis: The ARCHITECTURE.md system diagram (lines 29-70) depicts a pipeline of: Wallet Input → Next.js API Routes → OnchainOS CLI Wrapper → Pattern Classifier → Persona Engine. Six of eight conceptual pipeline stages exist as real code files. Two stages (TEE Attestation, x402 Payment) are self-declared [MOCK] and exist only as a static SVG badge and a fake setTimeout button respectively. The diagram itself is honest — it does NOT draw TEE or x402 boxes; but the implied 'full system' narrative that includes these stages overstates what is actually implemented.

component_map.note: Code exists and is well-structured with parsers, but in demo mode the analyze route short-circuits via cacheExists() check (analyze/route.ts line 12: `if (process.env.DEMO_MODE === 'true' || cacheExists())`). OnchainOS wrapper is never called at runtime.

ARCHITECTURE.md line 16 and Section 8 (line 1043) explicitly mark this as [MOCK]. Only a static 200x40 SVG with text '🔒 TEE-SECURED'. No live attestation generation, no TEE SDK, no MRENCLAVE verification. The Terminal.tsx header displays a hardcoded '🔒 TEE' badge and page.tsx shows a hardcoded 'ATTESTATION: 0x7f3a...b91e' span.

ARCHITECTURE.md line 17 and Section 9 (line 1080) explicitly mark as [MOCK]. PaymentButton.tsx uses a 1.5s setTimeout to fake a payment flow ('Processing x402...' → '✓ Payment Simulated'). No actual HTTP 402, no USDC settlement, no x402-sdk dependency.

22.2.title: Data flow honesty
22.2.analysis: Two key data-flow arrows are claimed or implied by the architecture narrative. (A) OnchainOS CLI ↔ OKX API Gateway: this connection is real but ONLY when the OnchainOS CLI binary is installed locally and the app runs in non-demo mode. In the actual demo deployment, neither condition holds — the cache path is always taken. (B) TEE Attestation → snapshot: this is a phantom arrow. The only TEE artifact is a static SVG badge (public/tee-badge.svg) with zero cryptographic content. There is no code that generates, verifies, or seals an attestation. The Terminal component renders a hardcoded hex string '0x7f3a...b91e' as a decorative badge — no data flows into or out of it.

arrow_audit.detail: The OnchainOS CLI binary, when installed, connects to OKX API Gateway via HTTPS (requires OKX_API_KEY env var). However: (1) the analyze route short-circuits to cache when DEMO_MODE=true or cache files exist (route.ts:12), (2) the OnchainOS CLI binary is not an npm dependency and would not exist in a Vercel/Next.js deployment. This arrow is real on a developer machine with the CLI installed but non-functional in the deployed demo.

22.3.title: Service boundary reality
22.3.analysis: The WIRE-REPORT.md and .wire-state.json describe 'OnchainOS CLI → OKX API Gateway' as a connection, and the README.md lists 'OnchainOS CLI (OKX API gateway)' as the data layer. This language implies a separate service boundary. In reality: (1) the ARCHITECTURE.md system diagram (lines 29-70) correctly shows OnchainOS CLI as an internal Next.js module (src/lib/onchainos.ts) using child_process.execSync, NOT a separate microservice; (2) the 'OKX API Gateway' is an external dependency of the OnchainOS CLI binary, not a service deployed or managed by Alter Ego; (3) there is no separate 'Onchainos MCP' process, Docker container, or sidecar — everything is a single Next.js monolith. The architecture is a monolithic Next.js app with pre-cached JSON data. The service-boundary implication in the wire report is aspirational/inflated.
22.3.actual_architecture: Single Next.js monolith. All four API routes (analyze, persona, compare, roast) are Next.js Route Handlers. The OnchainOS CLI wrapper is a library module (src/lib/onchainos.ts) that calls execSync. In demo mode, all data comes from pre-cached JSON files in src/data/cache/. No separate services, no MCP server, no API gateway deployed by this project.

22.4.title: Technology stack accuracy
22.4.analysis: ARCHITECTURE.md line 5 claims stack: 'Next.js 14, TypeScript 5, React 18, Tailwind CSS 3, Framer Motion 11, OnchainOS CLI'. The technology stack table (lines 74-82) lists OnchainOS as 'Blockchain data CLI' and 'Node child_process' as 'CLI execution'. However: (1) OnchainOS is a system CLI binary, not an npm package — it cannot be installed via `npm install` and would not exist in a standard Vercel deployment; (2) The versions in package.json differ: Next.js is 16.2.10 (not 14), React is 19.2.4 (not 18); (3) There is NO onchainos npm package, NO tee-sdk, NO x402-sdk in dependencies. The only runtime deps are next, react, react-dom, framer-motion. The ARCHITECTURE.md mentions Lucide React in the tech stack table but it is also absent from package.json dependencies. The stack claims are aspirational in key areas (TEE, x402, OnchainOS-as-service) and version-stale for the ones that do exist.

22.5.title: Scalability claim audit
22.5.analysis: ARCHITECTURE.md makes NO explicit scalability claims. Grep for 'scalable', 'distributed', 'serverless' across the full 2360-line document returned zero matches for those terms. The architecture is a single Next.js application — which is inherently serverless when deployed on Vercel, making the implicit serverless claim accurate. The data layer is static JSON files (src/data/cache/*.json) — which have no scaling concerns because they are read-once at request time from the filesystem. There is no database, no message queue, no cache cluster, no distributed coordination. The architecture is honest here: it doesn't overclaim scalability, and the actual deployment model (Next.js on Vercel) is genuinely serverless. The data being static JSON means scaling is a non-issue — the app would scale horizontally on Vercel's infrastructure without modification.

summary: The core pipeline (Wallet Input → API Routes → Classifier → Persona Engine → UI Components) is real and maps 1:1 to source files. The architecture document is admirably honest about its mocks: TEE Attestation and x402 Payment are explicitly marked [MOCK] in the Emergency Mode table. However, the technology stack version claims are stale (Next.js 14→16, React 18→19, Tailwind 3→4, Framer 11→12), and Lucide React is listed but absent. The OnchainOS CLI dependency is real code but is an undeclared system dependency (not in package.json) and is bypassed entirely in demo mode. No TEE SDK or x402 SDK exists. The architecture does not overclaim scalability. The service boundary narrative in ancillary files (WIRE-REPORT, README) implies a multi-service architecture, but the actual deployment is a single Next.js monolith serving static JSON. Overall gap between diagram and delivery: ~30% aspirational at the edges, 70% real in the core.
